<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                     </jats:title><jats:p>We consider the baby Skyrme model in a physically motivated limit of reaching the restricted or BPS baby Skyrme model, which is a model that enjoys area-preserving diffeomorphism invariance. The perturbation consists of the kinetic Dirichlet term with a small coefficient <jats:italic>ϵ</jats:italic> as well as the standard pion mass term, with coefficient <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \upepsilon {m}_1^2 $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>ϵ</mml:mi>
                  <mml:msubsup>
                    <mml:mi>m</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                    <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                  </mml:msubsup>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. The pions remain lighter than the soliton for any <jats:italic>ϵ</jats:italic> and therefore the model is physically acceptable, even in the <jats:italic>ϵ →</jats:italic> 0 limit. The version of the BPS baby Skyrme model we use has BPS solutions with Gaussian tails. We perform full numerical computations in the <jats:italic>ϵ →</jats:italic> 0 limit and even reach the strict <jats:italic>ϵ</jats:italic> = 0 case, finding new nontrivial BPS solutions, for which we do not yet know the analytic form.</jats:p>
title: Near-BPS baby Skyrmions with Gaussian tails
